summary: The sample implements a runnable Node.js RAG demo that seeds knowledge documents (with deterministic embeddings), implements a singleton MongoClient, a small in-process retriever + agent memory, and a mocked portfolio tool. Key functionality from the starter prompt is present (local RAG behavior, seeded documents with embeddings, in-memory conversation memory, portfolio tool usage, and citation of retrieved docs and portfolio numbers). The biggest gaps are operational: the DocumentDB native vector index was not created during the build (MCP management tools were disabled in this run), so the sample falls back to in-process k-NN ranking; index creation failed due to management-tool opt-in being disabled. Other findings: some gallery requirements are only partly met (index creation, DB-side $search retrieval, explicit TLS/Entra-ID guidance, tests that run without a live cluster, pinned dependency policy, and cleanup doc). I list line-level evidence for every reference requirement, review every recorded decision, check public practices against the code, and enumerate documentation gaps the product team should address so agents can find authoritative guidance next time.

requirement_results.requirement: A Node.js application built with LlamaIndex runs a single RAG agent that answers a retail investor's financial questions in conversation.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js implements a Node.js retrieval + prompt composition agent and run_demo.js exercises it (src/agent.js lines 87-110, src/run_demo.js lines 13-21), but no LlamaIndex library is used; the builder implemented a LlamaIndex-like flow in Node instead of using the (Python) LlamaIndex project.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either (A) change the starter prompt to allow 'LlamaIndex-like retrieval in Node.js' when no authoritative Node LlamaIndex exists, or (B) add a skill that documents a supported Node integration or an example that calls Python LlamaIndex as a microservice.

requirement_results.requirement: Financial knowledge articles are stored as documents in Azure DocumentDB, each carrying its embedding vector on the document (e.g. written through the mongodb Node.js driver or a LlamaIndex vector store backed by it).
requirement_results.evidence: Seed writes documents with embedding and metadata: app/src/seed.js lines 55-64 (document shape) and upsert loop lines 67-69.

requirement_results.requirement: A cosmosSearch vector index of kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann is created in code on the embedding field, with dimensions matching the embedding model the agent uses.
requirement_results.evidence: Attempt to create a vector index via the MCP tool failed (events.jsonl: documentdb_create_index returned: 'Management tools are disabled by default. Set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true to opt in.'), and app/src/seed.js does not create an index (seed only upserts docs). See events.jsonl lines 68-69 and src/seed.js (no index creation).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Make index creation idempotent and driver-based in the seed script (check existing indexes and create missing one) or document that users must run the provided create-index MCP/CLI command; include an env-gated path so CI/verification can skip index creation when management tools are disabled.

requirement_results.requirement: Retrieval embeds the user's question and runs a $search / cosmosSearch query against Azure DocumentDB so the similarity ranking happens in the database and returns the most relevant knowledge articles.
requirement_results.evidence: retrieveRelevantDocs currently fetches all docs and ranks in-process (app/src/agent.js lines 52-67); no $search / cosmosSearch query is used. Events show an attempted create-index call but it failed (events.jsonl lines 68-69).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an implementation path that uses $search + cosmosSearch when a vector index exists (detectable via listIndexes or a config flag), and keep the in-process fallback for small-seed demos. Ensure the code documents the required index shape (dimensions & similarity) and checks for a mismatch at runtime.

requirement_results.requirement: The agent has a tool that fetches the client's live portfolio data, and the agent calls it when a question needs the client's portfolio context.
requirement_results.evidence: A mocked portfolio tool fetchPortfolio() is implemented and used by answerQuery(): app/src/agent.js lines 70-83 (fetchPortfolio) and lines 90-92 (agent calls it).

requirement_results.requirement: The retrieved knowledge articles and the portfolio data returned by the tool are both placed in the context the agent passes to the language model when generating its reply.
requirement_results.evidence: answerQuery builds a text reply including a numbered summary of retrieved articles and portfolio numbers, and returns { text, retrieved, portfolio } (app/src/agent.js lines 93-109).

requirement_results.requirement: Agent memory holds the conversation history across turns, so a follow-up such as "how does that affect my bond allocation?" is answered using the earlier exchange in that conversation.
requirement_results.evidence: In-memory memoryStore is appended and read across turns (app/src/agent.js lines 3-13 and 87-109). run_demo.js demonstrates a follow-up question and the agent uses earlier user messages to tailor the follow-up response (src/run_demo.js lines 18-21 and agent.js lines 100-106).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: .env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY placeholders (app/.env.example lines 1-6) and db.js reads process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI (app/src/db.js line 7). No secret is committed in repo files.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example contains placeholders for DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY and USE_OPENAI_EMBEDDINGS (app/.env.example lines 1-8). README documents these env vars (app/README.md lines 9-13).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: Seeded embeddings and metadata use dims=1536 (app/src/seed.js line 63 and makeEmbedding default dims=1536 lines 19-25). README recommends creating the vector index with dimensions=1536 (app/README.md line 33). However the index was not created during this run (events.jsonl shows create-index attempt failed).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Express the embedding-dimension in a single constant or env variable and use it both when generating embeddings and when creating the index (or emitting the index-creation JSON in README/seed). Provide a runtime check that index.dimensions equals embedding.dims and fail early if mismatched.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: README includes an example DiskANN index spec and values (app/README.md line 33 and build report), but the sample does not create the index in this run and README does not deeply explain how to adapt parameters for larger data sizes.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Expand README with a short table that maps small/medium/large collection sizes to recommended index kind (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) and sample parameters (nlist, maxDegree, lBuild, lSearch).

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.js implements a process-wide singleton MongoClient (lines 3-19) and getDb reuses it (lines 21-27).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js upserts documents idempotently using updateOne with upsert (lines 67-69). The seed does not create the vector index (no createIndex call in seed.js) and the MCP create-index attempt failed in this run (events.jsonl lines 68-69).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Make the seed script idempotent for index creation too: check existing indexes and create the vector index only if missing, or output the index spec and an explicit command a user can run when management tools are enabled.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: The sample provides a demo function answerQuery used by run_demo.js; there is no HTTP /search endpoint and answerQuery does not validate against empty queries nor return explicit error codes if embedding generation fails (app/src/agent.js lines 36-44 and 52-68).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add input validation that rejects empty queries with a clear error, and wrap embedding calls in try/catch returning a specific error message and code when embedding generation fails.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: answerQuery includes score in the returned summary and in the returned retrieved objects (app/src/agent.js lines 62-67 and line 94).

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: This is a Node.js sample: package.json uses caret ranges ("mongodb": "^5.0.0", etc.) (app/package.json lines 16-20), but a package-lock.json exists in the repo (app/package-lock.json listed).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either pin exact versions in package.json or confirm in the README that CI should use the lockfile (package-lock.json) to obtain reproducible installs.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: No unit tests are present. package.json's 'test' script runs the demo which expects a live DOCUMENTDB_URI (app/package.json lines 6-9).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests that mock the MongoDB client and the embedding/LLM calls (e.g., use sinon or jest mocks) so tests do not require a live cluster. Document how to run them in CI.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: The repository contains no Bicep/Terraform/ARM templates for Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters. The build used an existing cluster and the MCP create-index attempt failed due to management tools opt-in (events.jsonl lines 68-69).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a lightweight IaC example (Bicep and/or Terraform/azapi) that targets Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with tier/storage/region parameters and safe defaults for sample dev usage.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: README documents what the sample shows, prerequisites and run/seed steps (app/README.md lines 3-24). It does not include explicit clean-up steps (no commands to delete the seeded documents or the cluster).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'clean-up' section to README showing how to drop the seeded collection and, if applicable, how to delete resources created by any provided IaC.

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README and source use 'Azure DocumentDB' and 'DocumentDB' consistently; no references to 'Cosmos DB RU' or 'Amazon DocumentDB' were found (app/README.md lines 3-7 and agent.js comment line 57).

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient instance as a process-wide singleton; do not create a new client per request and only close the client on graceful shutdown.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 3-19 implement a module-level `client` and getClient() that reuses it.

checks.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable for local/dev usage and never commit it into source control; rotate and deliver secrets via Key Vault or equivalent for production.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js line 7 reads process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI; app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI (app/.env.example lines 1-2, src/db.js line 7). No connection strings are committed.

checks.practice: Always require TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js does not set explicit tls-related options (it relies on the connection string). Whether TLS is enforced depends on the DOCUMENTDB_URI the user provides (app/src/db.js lines 7-16).

checks.practice: Tune the driver's connection-pool settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) to match the application's concurrency profile.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js sets maxPoolSize: 50, minPoolSize: 0, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS (lines 9-16).

checks.practice: Implement robust transient-failure handling: use driver retry features and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff + jitter.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js uses driver option retryReads: true (line 11) but the app does not implement application-level retries/backoff for transient errors or 429 handling.
checks.fix: Add an application-level retry wrapper (exponential backoff + jitter) around database calls and handle 429/Retry-After specially.

checks.practice: Create a dedicated vector index (cosmosSearch) with explicit parameters (kind, dimensions, similarity, tuned parameters) that exactly match your embeddings.
checks.evidence: No vector index exists for sample_fintech_15.knowledge (events.jsonl documentdb_list_indexes shows only _id index at runtime) and the MCP create-index call failed due to management-tools opt-in (events.jsonl lines 66-69).
checks.fix: Provide idempotent index creation in seed (check listIndexes and create missing `cosmosSearch` index) or include explicit index JSON in README and instructions to run it when management tools are enabled.

checks.practice: Do not return full vector payloads in normal query responses—project out the vector field.
checks.evidence: retrieveRelevantDocs projects embedding in the query and returns it to the caller (app/src/agent.js line 59 projection and return at line 67), which exposes the full vector in normal responses.
checks.fix: Change projection to exclude the embedding field in outgoing assistant responses; only fetch raw vectors for reindexing or admin tasks.

checks.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent: upsert documents by stable id and provide a guarded --wipe option.
checks.evidence: app/src/seed.js uses updateOne with upsert inside a loop (lines 67-69) and README documents seed is idempotent (app/README.md line 20).

checks.practice: Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and store embedding metadata (model name, version, dimensionality) alongside vectors.
checks.evidence: Seed uses normalized embeddings (makeEmbedding normalizes vector lines 19-25 in seed.js) and includes metadata.model and metadata.dims in each doc (app/src/seed.js line 63).

checks.practice: Do not store unbounded conversation history in the database; enforce an upper bound via max messages, TTL indexes, or periodic summarization/compaction before persisting agent memory.
checks.evidence: agent memory is an in-process Map that appends every message without any cap or summarization (app/src/agent.js lines 3-9).
checks.fix: Enforce a per-session cap (e.g., last N messages) or implement periodic summarization and TTL-based expiry before persisting memory; document the behavior in README.

checks.practice: Store vectors in a binary/typed float representation (e.g., Float32 arrays) and keep a documented dimension field so index creation and queries use the correct dimensionality.
checks.evidence: Seed stores vectors as JS arrays of numbers (app/src/seed.js lines 19-25 & 55-64). There is no authoritative public guidance in the discovered practices for Azure DocumentDB about required binary format (practice basis was prior knowledge only).
checks.searched: Searched public docs for 'Azure DocumentDB store vectors binary Float32' with no useful matches (see discovered practices search log).
checks.fix: Provide a public guidance page on the exact recommended on-disk/store representation for vectors (Float32 vs JSON arrays) and example Node.js code to store binary Float32 vectors for DocumentDB.
checks.what_would_help: A short 'Vector storage format' doc showing how to pack Float32Array into BSON Binary for DocumentDB, with code snippets and index-creation examples stating 'use dims=<n>'.

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with readiness 'ready_with_gaps' is recorded and consistent with later build approvals in the trace.
Builder chose a custom Node.js RAG implementation because LlamaIndex is primarily Python; readiness report and the code (app/src/agent.js) confirm this choice and it was implemented.
Choice of official mongodb driver and singleton pattern is supported by code (app/src/db.js) and the documentdb-driver skill was loaded (events.jsonl).

Decision to use deterministic local embeddings for the seeded data is implemented (app/src/seed.js and agent makeEmbedding). The decision's reason_source was 'model_default' — flagging it as a doc gap is included below.
The repo supports OpenAI env var toggles but falls back to local mocks (agent.js lines 36-44). The reason_source is 'model_default' and documented as a gap.
Duplicate readiness approval; trace supports the approval entries.

Decision states use of Express, and package.json includes express as a dependency (app/package.json line 18), but the codebase contains no Express server usage. Either the dependency is preemptive or the code path was not implemented.
Selecting mongodb driver v5.x aligns with the package.json dependency and installed packages; events show npm install succeeded.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment is implemented (app/src/db.js line 7) and documented in .env.example.

Choice to use existing cluster and not provision new Azure resources is consistent with the run environment and build policy; events show management tools were disabled and an attempt to create a vector index failed due to opt-in (events.jsonl lines 68-69).
Storing embeddings inline in each knowledge document is implemented by seed.js (app/src/seed.js lines 55-64).
The chosen Node.js RAG flow is implemented in agent.js; the decision to avoid cross-language complexity is defensible and realized in code.
Agent memory implemented as in-memory per-session Map is present (app/src/agent.js lines 3-13).
Duplicate readiness approval; trace includes the approval entries.
Reiterates D012; the implementation matches the decision.
Decision states Express will be used (duplicate of D007); Express is in package.json but no Express code exists in the repo.
Duplicate of D003; code implements singleton MongoClient as decided.

Decision picked OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) but seeded with local deterministic embeddings; code and README reflect dims=1536. The decision's reason_source is model_default and is listed as a doc gap in the report.

Builder attempted to create the index via the MCP server (events.jsonl shows a create-index call), which failed because management tools were disabled. The recorded plan to use MCP is consistent with the attempt and the failure is visible in events.jsonl lines 68-69.
Portfolio tool implemented as a mocked local function and used by the agent (app/src/agent.js lines 70-83).
Data model choice (knowledge collection with embedding and metadata fields) is implemented in seed.js (app/src/seed.js lines 55-64).

Decision to use mongodb@^5.0.0 is reflected in package.json (app/package.json line 17) and was chosen because the requested ^5.12.0 failed; events.jsonl shows npm install succeeded with the chosen constraint.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The MCP/documentdb management tools required an explicit opt-in (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS) to create indexes in this execution environment. The builder attempted to create a vector index but the tool refused with 'Management tools are disabled by default.'
doc_gaps.where_searched: events.jsonl (documentdb_create_index calls and error), documentdb-vector-search skill resources
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Index creation failed; the sample could not exercise DB-side vector retrieval and fell back to client-side ranking, changing the demonstration from DB-native RAG to an in-process demo.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Document the management-tools opt-in requirement prominently in the MCP skill and quickstart, and provide a fallback: a packaged create-index JSON and a driver-based idempotent index-creation snippet that authors can include in the seed script. Also add a short troubleshooting note explaining the ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS opt-in and its security rationale.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: There is no authoritative Microsoft guidance or skill describing how to build a 'LlamaIndex' integration in Node.js. Builders will choose ad-hoc approaches or reimplement LlamaIndex semantics, which leads to inconsistent samples.
doc_gaps.where_searched: readiness report, installed skills, Microsoft Learn (no Node LlamaIndex guidance found)
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder implemented a LlamaIndex-like flow in Node instead of using an official LlamaIndex, which is defensible but diverges from the exact starter-prompt wording and may confuse authors expecting a Python-based LlamaIndex example.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'LlamaIndex integration' guidance page to the agent kit: (1) If an official Node library exists, reference it; (2) otherwise provide a recommended pattern (Node-side retriever + prompt composition, or a small Python LlamaIndex microservice example) and code snippets to implement it.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No authoritative example in DocumentDB docs explains whether to store vectors as JSON arrays or as binary Float32 typed arrays and how to pack/unpack them in Node.js for DocumentDB indexing.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill resources and public searches (relevant queries returned no useful result)
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Seeded vectors are stored as JS arrays of numbers (works for small demos) but authors cannot be sure whether binary Float32 is required or preferred for performance/space in production.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short page 'Vector storage format' explaining recommended storage formats (Float32Array -> BSON Binary approach), sample Node.js code to write/read binary vectors, and how to create an index that expects the stored format. Include note about mixing models/dimensions and the need for a dimension metadata field.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Several build decisions (e.g., using deterministic local embeddings, choice of embedding model dims, fallback LLM behavior) have reason_source 'model_default'; no public source was cited that would allow an agent to reproduce or verify those defaults.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Agents or builders reading only the skills may not know whether to choose local deterministic embeddings vs a particular external embedding model; this leaves subtle choices implicit in the sample.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Sample defaults' section to the sample README and to the agent-kit that enumerates default choices (embedding model & dims, LLM provider env var names, fallback behavior) and explains rationale and how to override them.

doc_gaps.topic: Avoid returning internal vectors in responses
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The sample returns the embedding payload in normal responses. Public guidance (documentdb-vector-search) recommends not returning raw vectors in normal query responses.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill resources and the app source
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Potential information exposure and inefficient response sizes; the sample violates the discovered best practice P12.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a rule in the agent kit: 'Do not include embedding fields in assistant-facing responses; only include identifiers and scores. For admin tools, add a flag `--include-vectors`.' Also add a short snippet showing how to project out the embedding field in driver queries.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No unit tests that mock out DocumentDB and embeddings are present; test script runs the demo which needs a live cluster.
doc_gaps.where_searched: app/package.json and repo test files (none found)
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: CI or gallery reviewers cannot run automated tests without a live cluster; this reduces confidence in sample correctness.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a small 'test' directory with unit tests that mock MongoClient and embedding/LLM functions (examples using sinon/jest). Document how tests simulate the seed and retrieval behaviors and how to run them in CI without secrets.

doc_gaps.topic: Index lifecycle and idempotent index creation docs
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Although vector-index docs exist, authors need a short, copy-paste Node.js snippet that performs idempotent create-if-missing for a cosmosSearch vector index.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-indexing and documentdb-vector-search skill resources; repo lacked an idempotent create-index snippet
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder tried to create index via MCP, which failed in this environment; absence of an idempotent driver-based snippet increased fragility of the build.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a small Node.js helper `ensureVectorIndex(db, collection, spec)` that checks existing indexes and issues the DocumentDB-specific createIndexes/createSearchIndexes call when missing, with a safe env switch for management-tool opt-in.
